brief: Deutsche Bank's September chartbook (Jim Reid) frames the bond sell-off as normalisation rather than stress. US nominal GDP at 6.6% yoy sits about 180bps above 10yr yields, so if nominal growth settles at 5.5% a 4.8% yield is historically average, and at 6% around 5.3% is reasonable. Higher coupons keep total returns positive, with the US Treasury index up nearly 15% since yields peaked in October 2023. From there the note asks whether the Fed should hike. Core PCE is 15bps off a 34-year high ex-pandemic, trend inflation is sticky near 3%, financial conditions are the loosest since 1990, policy sits below rules after last year's insurance cuts, and payrolls have turned up in 2026, so those cuts look ripe to be reversed. Energy costs pushed the ECB's real deposit rate negative and DB economists expect a hike this week and another to 2.75% in December. Democrats have closed the Senate gap since the Iran strikes, correlating with Brent. Q2 global earnings growth was the strongest on record outside the pandemic, driven by an AI capex boom where the top five spenders outspend the other 495 combined. The yen is bouncing off 40-year lows after 15.4tn yen of intervention.
